title: The Inhaler, the Pneumonia, and a Clot in the Lung

questions.stem: An adolescent or adult with asthma. As-needed rescue medicine alone:

options.text: Is not a plan; an inhaled corticosteroid belongs in the regimen
Replaces a bronchodilator in chronic obstructive disease

questions.explanation: Every adolescent and adult with asthma gets a steroid in the inhaler.

questions.stem: Mild chronic obstructive disease, few symptoms, no hospital exacerbation. Start with:

options.text: An inhaled corticosteroid as the first and only drug
A long-acting bronchodilator, muscarinic type preferred, not an inhaled steroid first

questions.explanation: This group starts a long-acting bronchodilator. The long-acting muscarinic type is preferred, not an inhaled corticosteroid.

questions.stem: A chronic obstructive exacerbation typically gets:

options.text: A short systemic steroid; antibiotics only when they are indicated
No medicine if the x-ray is clear

questions.explanation: A flare gets a short steroid course. Antibiotics are selective.

options.text: Where to treat, using severity, not a single lab
Whether to start a sugar-spilling diabetes pill

questions.stem: Severe community pneumonia is treated with:

options.text: Two drugs: a beta-lactam plus a macrolide, or a beta-lactam plus a fluoroquinolone
Anaerobic coverage in every mild case

questions.stem: Straightforward aspiration pneumonia. Routine anaerobic coverage is:

options.text: A reason to skip site-of-care decisions

questions.explanation: Anaerobic coverage is not automatic for straightforward aspiration.

questions.stem: A pulmonary embolus with a normal blood pressure. Treatment is:

options.text: No treatment if the x-ray is clear

questions.explanation: A stable embolus is treated with anticoagulation. Do not lyse a stable embolus.

questions.stem: Systemic thrombolysis for pulmonary embolism is for:

options.text: Every embolus, including a normal blood pressure
A small early drop in filtration

questions.explanation: A lytic is for shock, not for a normal pressure.

questions.stem: The diabetes medicine that spills sugar in the urine should be held when the patient is:

options.text: Stable in clinic with a small early drop in filtration, forever
Fasting, in surgery, or critically ill

questions.explanation: Hold it for fasting, surgery, or critical illness because of ketoacidosis risk.

questions.stem: A small early drop in filtration after starting that sugar-spilling medicine:

options.text: Means the drug must be stopped forever
Is not, by itself, a reason to stop it forever
Is an indication for a lytic

questions.explanation: That early dip is not an automatic lifelong stop.
